name: 4-Hour Body diet

card.summary: Tim Ferriss's slow-carb diet of meat, legumes and vegetables with a weekly cheat day, used to lose body fat and look leaner.
card.note: Critics have questioned the weekly cheat day and long-term sustainability.

quick.overview:
The 4-Hour Body diet is the slow-carb eating plan from Tim Ferriss's 2010 book The 4-Hour Body. It centers on repeated simple meals of protein, legumes and vegetables, avoids starches, sweets and fruit, and allows one day a week of unrestricted eating.

People use it to lose body fat and get a leaner physique. Hacker News users posted personal reviews of it, such as a 2011 "2.2 month review".
quick.how: Followers eat a small set of repeating meals built around meat, beans and vegetables, skip bread, rice and sweets during the week, and eat freely one day each week. Food lists circulate online, including a 2018 Hacker News post.
quick.risks: Reviewers quoted by WebMD, Harvard Business Review and U.S. News questioned its long-term practicality and the cheat day. Anyone with a medical condition would normally consult a clinician before changing diet.

lead: The 4-Hour Body diet, also called the slow-carb diet, is the eating plan described in Tim Ferriss's 2010 book The 4-Hour Body, published by Crown. [1] Its rules, as summarized on Wikipedia, are to eat a small set of simple meals repeatedly, favor slow carbohydrates and take one cheat day each week. [1]

The diet avoids starches, sweets, fruit and artificial sweeteners, and emphasizes lean protein and a few vegetables. [1] Followers use it as a route to fat loss and a leaner look, and online readers have posted weight-loss logs and food lists. [2][3]
The book reached number one on the New York Times bestseller list. Reviewers were divided, with some praising its avoidance of refined carbohydrates and others questioning its sustainability. [1]

chain: Eat repeated protein, legume and vegetable meals
Lose body fat for a leaner look
angle.text: The plan is used to lose weight, which makes the face and body look leaner. The weekly cheat day is part of the design.

infobox: Repeat meals, slow carbs, weekly cheat day

paras: Per Wikipedia, the book runs 592 pages and covers diet, exercise, sleep and sexual performance, with diet as the main focus. [1] The diet itself is a short list of rules rather than a calorie-counting method. [1]

WebMD's review was skeptical but praised avoiding refined carbs and repeating meals; Barry Sears questioned long-term practicality and Michael Aziz called the cheat day "dangerous", according to Wikipedia. [1] A Harvard Business Review piece quoted Tieraona Low Dog as expecting weight loss for many but doubting every claim. [1] The New York Times review was harshly critical. [1]
A 2011 Hacker News post offered a 2.2-month personal review of the diet, and a 2018 post shared a food list. [2][3]
No studies found. The diet is not specifically addressed by the U.S. Dietary Guidelines. [1]

timeline.event: The 4-Hour Body is published and debuts at number one on the New York Times list. [1]
A personal 2.2-month slow-carb review is posted on Hacker News. [2]
